(2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Tokens loaded from storage never get token_expiry_time recomputed, so is_token_valid() treats a stale/expired stored access token as valid, the proactive-refresh path is skipped, and the client ends up forcing a full re-authorization instead of a silent refresh after every restart. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both target the same reported bug — #2875's own inline comment explicitly names the missing token_expiry_time recompute on load as its motivation. #1784 fixes it at the source with a 3-line change in _initialize() plus a new expired_tokens regression fixture proving expiry is recomputed on load. #2875 instead adds a reactive fallback inside the 401 branch of async_auth_flow (try stored refresh_token before full re-auth) that only exists to work around the same gap; once #1784 closes that gap, the proactive-refresh branch fires before any 401 occurs in the scenario #2875 describes, making its added branch redundant for the case it cites.

prs.title: fix: skip JSON pre-parsing for str union annotations in pre_parse_json
prs.author: adityuhkapoor
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json() only skipped JSON pre-parsing when a parameter's annotation was exactly `str`. For any Union that includes `str` (e.g. `str | None`, `str | int`), it still ran `json.loads()` on string inputs, corrupting legitimate string values that happen to look like JSON (e.g. "null", "123", a JSON-looking string meant to stay a plain string). (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json() only skipped JSON pre-parsing when a parameter's annotation was exactly `str`. For any Union that includes `str` (e.g. `str | None`, `str | int`), it still ran `json.loads()` on string inputs, corrupting legitimate string values that happen to look like JSON (e.g. "null", "123", a JSON-looking string meant to stay a plain string). (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs patch the exact same conditional in pre_parse_json() to stop mis-parsing string values under str-containing unions. #2032 generalizes the fix via a `_SIMPLE_TYPES` frozenset + `_should_pre_parse_json()` helper that skips pre-parsing for any union composed solely of str/int/float/bool/None, which already covers the `str | None` case #3056 targets plus additional shapes like `str | int` and `str | bool` that #3056 does not address. #3056 is narrower in scope (Optional[str] only) but does add one thing #2032's diff lacks: unwrapping `Annotated[...]` on individual union members before the type check. That gap is a minor edge case (Annotated is normally applied to the whole union, not a single arm) and can be folded into #2032's helper if needed, whereas #3056's fix would still leave `str | int`/`str | float` unions mis-parsed.

prs.title: Fix substring matches in WWW-Authenticate parsing
prs.author: Whning0513
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same bug in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py: WWW-Authenticate header parsing (used to extract Bearer challenge parameters like resource_metadata) incorrectly did substring/naive matching on the raw header string instead of properly tokenizing it into individual auth-params, causing false matches and mis-parsing when quoted param values contain commas or when parameter names are substrings of other tokens. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same bug in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py: WWW-Authenticate header parsing (used to extract Bearer challenge parameters like resource_metadata) incorrectly did substring/naive matching on the raw header string instead of properly tokenizing it into individual auth-params, causing false matches and mis-parsing when quoted param values contain commas or when parameter names are substrings of other tokens. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both add a quote-aware, comma-splitting tokenizer at the same insertion point in utils.py, but PR #3041 additionally isolates the Bearer challenge by scheme before extracting its auth-params (_extract_bearer_auth_params checks segment.partition(' ') for an exact 'bearer' scheme token), so it correctly handles headers containing more than one challenge (e.g. 'DPoP ..., Bearer ...'). PR #3012's _iter_www_auth_params only strips the header's first space-delimited token once and treats everything after it as one flat parameter list, so it would merge parameters from a second challenge into the first if the header contains multiple schemes. #3041's diff is also more complete (two cooperating helpers: segment-splitting + scheme-aware extraction) covering both the comma/quote-splitting defect and the scheme-substring-matching defect described in its title, versus #3012's single generic tokenizer plus an unrelated `import re` cleanup.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs touch the same failure path (max reconnection attempts exceeded in _handle_reconnection), but with different mechanisms and blast radius. #2395 sends a JSONRPCError directly through ctx.read_stream_writer, scoped to the specific pending JSONRPCRequest — this reuses the same INTERNAL_ERROR/ErrorData/JSONRPCError pattern that #3092 independently uses elsewhere in this file for non-2xx responses, showing it's the established idiom for this class of bug. #3098 instead adds a new _unwrap_exception helper that recursively searches anyio ExceptionGroups to re-raise a StreamableHTTPError, which changes the exception type propagated at the task-group/context-manager level (a wider behavioral change affecting all callers, not just the failed request) and also includes an unrelated change reverting `from __future__ import annotations as _annotations` back to a plain import, suggesting the diff isn't fully isolated to the stated fix. #2395 is the smaller, more contained change that resolves the same symptom.

clusters.pick_reason: Both add a quote-aware, comma-splitting tokenizer at the same insertion point in utils.py, but PR #3041 additionally isolates the Bearer challenge by scheme before extracting its auth-params (_extract_bearer_auth_params checks segment.partition(' ') for an exact 'bearer' scheme token), so it correctly handles headers containing more than one challenge (e.g. 'DPoP ..., Bearer ...'). PR #3012's _iter_www_auth_params only strips the header's first space-delimited token once and treats everything after it as one flat parameter list, so it would merge parameters from a second challenge into the first if the header contains multiple schemes. #3041's diff is also more complete (two cooperating helpers: segment-splitting + scheme-aware extraction) covering both the comma/quote-splitting defect and the scheme-substring-matching defect described in its title, versus #3012's single generic tokenizer plus an unrelated `import re` cleanup.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs patch the exact same conditional in pre_parse_json() to stop mis-parsing string values under str-containing unions. #2032 generalizes the fix via a `_SIMPLE_TYPES` frozenset + `_should_pre_parse_json()` helper that skips pre-parsing for any union composed solely of str/int/float/bool/None, which already covers the `str | None` case #3056 targets plus additional shapes like `str | int` and `str | bool` that #3056 does not address. #3056 is narrower in scope (Optional[str] only) but does add one thing #2032's diff lacks: unwrapping `Annotated[...]` on individual union members before the type check. That gap is a minor edge case (Annotated is normally applied to the whole union, not a single arm) and can be folded into #2032's helper if needed, whereas #3056's fix would still leave `str | int`/`str | float` unions mis-parsed.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs touch the same failure path (max reconnection attempts exceeded in _handle_reconnection), but with different mechanisms and blast radius. #2395 sends a JSONRPCError directly through ctx.read_stream_writer, scoped to the specific pending JSONRPCRequest — this reuses the same INTERNAL_ERROR/ErrorData/JSONRPCError pattern that #3092 independently uses elsewhere in this file for non-2xx responses, showing it's the established idiom for this class of bug. #3098 instead adds a new _unwrap_exception helper that recursively searches anyio ExceptionGroups to re-raise a StreamableHTTPError, which changes the exception type propagated at the task-group/context-manager level (a wider behavioral change affecting all callers, not just the failed request) and also includes an unrelated change reverting `from __future__ import annotations as _annotations` back to a plain import, suggesting the diff isn't fully isolated to the stated fix. #2395 is the smaller, more contained change that resolves the same symptom.

members.author: Bartok9

clusters.pick_reason: Both add a quote-aware, comma-splitting tokenizer at the same insertion point in utils.py, but PR #3041 additionally isolates the Bearer challenge by scheme before extracting its auth-params (_extract_bearer_auth_params checks segment.partition(' ') for an exact 'bearer' scheme token), so it correctly handles headers containing more than one challenge (e.g. 'DPoP ..., Bearer ...'). PR #3012's _iter_www_auth_params only strips the header's first space-delimited token once and treats everything after it as one flat parameter list, so it would merge parameters from a second challenge into the first if the header contains multiple schemes. #3041's diff is also more complete (two cooperating helpers: segment-splitting + scheme-aware extraction) covering both the comma/quote-splitting defect and the scheme-substring-matching defect described in its title, versus #3012's single generic tokenizer plus an unrelated `import re` cleanup.
